propositions: A TOCTOU race in completion close reads HEAD independently during verify and sign steps, allowing an unrelated commit to land between them and invalidate the attestation window.

When verify succeeds on HEAD revision A but sign observes HEAD revision B (due to concurrent commit), the ticket closes without a completion signature despite the refusal to attest, leaving no recovery path via re-close.
The current default (no --ref) path reads HEAD twice and remains vulnerable to drift-induced unsigned closes, while the --ref path only pins coherence for verify and sign but not the full close unit.
The suggested recovery message ('Re-close to certify') is a no-op for already-closed tickets, and only --force-close or manual manifest fabrication remain viable but unacceptable.
Completion close must either pin a single verified revision for the entire verify+sign+close sequence, or abort the close on drift and leave the ticket in_progress for retry.
A first-class non-force recovery mechanism is needed to obtain completion attestation for a closed-but-unsigned ticket.
